summary: Most nationalities simply buy a US$30 visa on arrival, good for 30 days, when landing at Dili's airport or seaport, while EU citizens enter visa-free for up to 90 days under a bilateral agreement. Arriving overland from Indonesia requires a visa or visa application authorisation arranged in advance.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Timor-Leste.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

travelInsurance.text: Not required for entry, but strongly advisable with medical-evacuation cover — hospitals are basic and serious cases are evacuated to Darwin or Singapore.

onwardTicket.text: Not systematically checked, but airlines and border officers may ask for evidence of onward travel — carry your return booking.

proofOfFunds.text: Border officers may ask visitors to show means of support for their stay; no fixed amount is consistently enforced — carry some US dollars in cash.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of US$10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

notes: Duty-free allowances are modest (roughly 200 cigarettes and a small quantity of alcohol per adult) — declare anything beyond personal use.

payments.text: Timor-Leste uses the US dollar. Cards are accepted only at a few hotels and supermarkets in Dili, and ATMs are scarce and unreliable outside the capital — bring clean, small-denomination dollar notes, as change for large bills is hard to find.

safety.text: Timor-Leste is generally calm and visitors are warmly received. Petty theft occurs in Dili, roads are poor, medical facilities are basic, and political gatherings occasionally turn tense and are best avoided. Saltwater crocodiles are a real hazard on many beaches — ask locally before swimming.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The May–October dry season brings the best roads, trekking and world-class diving around Atauro Island; the wet season (roughly November–April) can cut off rural roads.

tips.text: Have US$30 in cash ready for the visa on arrival — cards are not accepted at the immigration counter, and small bills are easier for any change.

The US$30 visa on arrival is issued only at Dili's airport and seaport. If you plan to cross overland from Indonesian West Timor (Batugade/Motaain), arrange a visa or visa application authorisation with the Migration Service or a Timorese embassy first.
Outside Dili, roads are rough and public transport minimal — hire a 4WD (ideally with driver) for mountain districts, and allow far more time than distances suggest.
Malaria and dengue occur year-round — use repellent and consider prophylaxis for rural stays. Bring any medication you need; pharmacies outside Dili are very limited.
Atauro Island, a short boat ride from Dili, sits on some of the world's most biodiverse reefs — dry-season visibility is superb, and community homestays make an easy overnight trip.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Timor-Leste?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do not need anything in advance when flying in: a US$30 visa on arrival, valid 30 days, is issued at Dili's airport and seaport. EU citizens go one better — visa-free for up to 90 days under the EU–Timor-Leste agreement. Only overland arrivals need paperwork beforehand.

faq.question: What do I need for the visa on arrival?
faq.answer: A passport valid for 6 months, US$30 in cash, and ideally a return or onward booking and accommodation details. The visa is stamped on the spot at Presidente Nicolau Lobato International Airport or the Dili seaport.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Timor-Leste?
faq.answer: Yes — apply at the Migration Service in Dili before your visa expires. Extensions are granted in 30-day blocks (roughly US$35 each), generally up to 90 days in total. Confirm current fees with the Migration Service.

faq.question: What currency does Timor-Leste use?
faq.answer: The US dollar is the official currency (with local centavo coins). Bring cash — cards work only in a few Dili establishments, and ATMs are unreliable. Small, clean bills are the most practical.

faq.question: Can I cross overland from Indonesia to Timor-Leste?
faq.answer: Yes, via the Batugade/Motaain crossing from West Timor, but the visa on arrival is not available there — arrange a visa or visa application authorisation in advance through the Migration Service (migracao.gov.tl) or a Timorese embassy such as the one in Kupang.
